# NIGHT SHIFT, SUBLEVEL THREE. WRITING THIS WHILE I STILL BELIEVE IT. [color=#5E7066]Pinned at the request of readers. The opening post is long. Read all of it before you reply.[/color]
### #1 lights_out_orderly (OP) // 83.05.01 I am an orderly. Nights, sublevel three, participant corridor. My job is trays, linen, and sitting at the desk at the end of the corridor watching a screen that shows twelve doors. I took it because it paid double and because nobody else would take it, which I should have thought about longer.
Room fourteen was a man about my age. Debt relief form, I think. He was funny. He used to read the tray menu out loud through the door slot in a fancy voice, like it was a restaurant. Every night when I collected his tray I said [italic]goodnight, fourteen,[/italic] and every night he said it back, [italic]goodnight, orderly,[/italic] like we were in a play.
Phase one he was just hungry. He ate everything and asked for more. He said, and I wrote it down after because it bothered me, that [italic]the meat tastes right.[/italic] Not good. Right.
Phase two he got pale. Not sick pale. Pale like something left out of the light. He shivered all the time, even with the heating up, and he stopped reading the menu.
Phase three they started injections. A tech came in at 0200 with a cold case and a guard. After the injections his veins showed dark under his skin, all the way up his neck. He told me his skin felt too tight. He told me his teeth hurt. He stopped saying goodnight back.
Phase four they put the second lock on. I could hear him through the door, and it did not sound like a man in pain. It sounded like a man being folded. Bones. Grinding, like stones under a cart. On the screen he was curled in the corner and he looked longer than he should have, his arms reaching past his knees.
I came on shift on the night after the door was ticked five and room fourteen was empty. The restraint straps were on the floor, not unbuckled. Snapped. A team in white suits was cleaning the walls.
I sat at the desk and did my rounds and around three in the morning, from the vent above my desk, I heard my own voice say [italic]goodnight, fourteen.[/italic]
My voice. My tired, end of shift voice, exactly the way I say it. I had not said anything. I was alone.
### #2 shift_guard_ii // 83.05.01 I believe you. I am not going to say why yet.
### #3 just_a_pig // 83.05.02 Is it possible you heard a recording? Monitoring picks up everything in that corridor. Somebody playing back a tape to scare the new staff?
### #4 lights_out_orderly (OP) // 83.05.02 I have thought about that every hour since. The corridor speakers are on the ceiling. This came from the vent, and it moved. The second time it was further down the duct.
### #5 shift_guard_ii // 83.05.03 All right. Here is why.
Our site had a room emptied last year. A week later we were told a [italic]transferred participant[/italic] would be moved through the lower dock under escort, and to keep the corridor clear and not look. I looked.
It walked. On two legs, like a person, but bent forward at the top because it was taller than the door frame and did not want to touch it. Thin. You could count every rib from across the dock. Long arms, long fingers. The skin was the colour of a candle. The eyes gave off a little light, the way an animal's eyes do in a torch beam, except there was no torch.
When it went past me it turned its head and breathed in. Long and slow. The way you breathe in over a pot of stew.
On its back, burned into the skin like a brand on a crate, was the Company logo. The whole word. Weyland-Yutani. Someone did that to it on purpose.
### #6 graveyard_cook // 83.05.04 The trays for the emptied rooms do not stop. They go up from sublevel three to a dock door twice as big, on a cart, at night. Five kilos a time. The cart comes back with the tray bent.
### #7 shift_guard_ii // 83.05.04 One more thing. It did not have an escort the way you would escort a prisoner. One handler walked in front of it, a woman from the research wing, and it followed her. Close. Like a dog follows the person who feeds it. Nobody had a gun pointed at it. Everyone had a gun pointed at the floor near it, which is not the same thing.
A tech told me later that the conditioning takes on most of them. That whoever is there when it opens its eyes is the one it listens to. And that when the conditioning does not take, they do not talk about what happens to whoever was there.
### #8 duty_cycle (mod) // 83.05.04 lights_out_orderly, please stop posting from anywhere near your site. Change terminals. If you can quit, quit. Do not tell anyone at work about this thread.
Everyone else: no site names in replies. If what is in this thread is true, the Company will want to know which corridor it came from more than it will want to deny it.
### #9 floor_polish // 83.05.09 We have the phase sheets on our doors too. I never knew what the five boxes meant. I wish I still did not.
### #10 debt_and_dust // 83.05.12 My cousin said the food was strange but he could not get enough of it.
I need someone to tell me this is a different programme.
